content: Chimaphila umbellata, also known as Umbellate Wintergreen, Pipsissewa, or Prince's Pine, is a small perennial flowering plant that thrives in dry woodlands or sandy soils. It is native to the cool temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. The plant typically grows to a height of 10 to 35 cm and features evergreen, shiny, bright green leaves. These leaves are arranged in opposite pairs or whorls of three to four along the stem. The leaves have shallowly toothed margins, with fine hairs present at the tips of the teeth. The flowers of Chimaphila umbellata are either white or pink and are borne in small umbels, each containing four to eight flowers. Although the plant maintains green leaves throughout the year, it derives a significant portion of its nutrition from soil fungi. This makes it a partial myco-heterotroph, a trait it shares with related plants such as those in the Pyrola genus, which are also partial or full myco-heterotrophs. There are four recognized subspecies of Chimaphila umbellata: Chimaphila umbellata subsp. umbellata, found in Europe and Asia. Chimaphila umbellata subsp. acuta, native to southwestern North America. Chimaphila umbellata subsp. cisatlantica, found in northeastern North America. Chimaphila umbellata subsp. occidentalis, native to northwestern North America. The plant has been used as a flavoring agent in candies and soft drinks, particularly in root beer. The name Pipsissewa originates from the Cree language and translates to it-breaks-into-small-pieces. Additionally, the name Pipsissewa is used for a character in the Uncle Wiggly books by Howard R. Garis.
